item.title: Houston high school football playoffs: 15 players who could make a huge impact
item.description: Randle running back Landen William-Callis has rushed for 2,477 yards. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) The Houston high school football playoffs have arrived, and several of the area's top players will have a chance to make their mark on the postseason. From Randle running back Landen Williams-Callis chasing state history to standout quarterbacks, explosive offensive playmakers and game-wreckers, on defense, the Houston area is loaded with talent. North Shore, Katy, Bridgeland, Cypress Ranch and other contenders have plenty of star power, but a few individual performances could ultimately determine which teams make deep playoff runs. Here are 15 players to watch as the road to the state championships begins. Landen Williams-Callis, RB, Randle Williams-Callis has already made plenty of history this season, but another deep playoff run with the Lions could further his legacy as one of the greatest all-time players in Texas high school football history. The five-star Texas commit has rushed for 2,477 yards and 37 touchdowns this season while averaging 12.1 yards per carry. He's rushed for 200-plus in all but one game and capped the regular season with 207 yards and four touchdowns during a 31-14 victory over Friendswood. He'll obviously be the focal point of the Randle offense as the Lions pursue a third consecutive state championship game appearance and their first in Class 5A Division I. Rushing for 247.7 yards per game this season, Williams-Callis is currently on pace to break the state's all-time mark with six more games. He enters the playoffs with 9,971 career rushing yards, fifth all-time behind Kaegan Ash (11,382), Kenneth Hall (11,232), Johnathan Gray (10,889) and Traylon Shead (10,292). Bridgeland running back Kash Schwab has scored 29 touchdowns. (Kirk Sides/Houston Chronicle) Kash Schwab, RB, Bridgeland For the third time in four years, Bridgeland finished the regular season 9-1 with an undefeated district championship. Schwab has a lot to do with that accomplishment as he's been the catalyst for the Bears' offense since his breakout sophomore campaign. Schwab is one of four active Houston-area players to clear 5,000 career rushing yards, joining Williams-Callis, La Porte's Sean Simon and Kinkaid's Wayne Shanks Jr. The senior UNLV commit gives Bridgeland a dangerous and versatile weapon out of the backfield as the team embarks on the Class 6A Division I playoff bracket. The Bears suffered a first-round exit against Klein Collins last season, but Schwab was a difference-maker during the program's run to a regional championship game in 2024. He's piled up more than 1,800 all-purpose yards and 29 total touchdowns this season, already his best in a Bridgeland uniform. Cypress Ranch quarterback Braden Baker is completing 74.7% of his passes. item.title: Dakorien Moore Points Out Empty Ohio State Seats After Big Win
item.description: Oregon Ducks wide receiver Dakorien Moore (1) celebrates a touchdown during the NCAA football game against the Ohio State Buckeyes at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Nov. 7, 2026. Ohio State lost 41-28. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oregon wide receiver Dakorien Moore stated that the Ohio State crowd started with 103,000 people but ended with less than half that number after the Ducks defeated the Buckeyes 41-28 on Saturday. He told reporters that his team expected the stands to empty as they took a commanding lead in the fourth quarter. Moore focused on executing his plays rather than worrying about the fans who walked out during the game. The Ducks secured a massive upset in Columbus, improving their record to 6-3 with this victory. According to a report , Moore led the team in receiving with seven catches for 56 yards and a touchdown. His performance included a one-handed grab that became a key moment in the second-half shellacking of the host team. This win keeps Oregon in the hunt for a Big Ten title and a spot in the College Football Playoff. Moore on the Empty Seats Moore did not let the silence of the crowd distract him from the task at hand. He explained that his only goal was to play for the teammate standing next to him. “Just going out there executing, we knew the stands were gonna look like that every time,” Moore said. He noted that the fans left early as the score gap grew too wide to ignore. The sophomore receiver has now surpassed his total reception count from last season after just nine games. Evan Stewart and Jeremiah McClellan have missed time, leaving Moore to carry a heavier load. His production has helped his new starting quarterback, Dylan Raiola, find his rhythm. Raiola threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Ohio State. The quarterback’s confidence has grown significantly since his struggles in an earlier start against UCLA. Season Totals and Playoff Hopes Entering Saturday’s game, Moore had already surpassed his season total from the previous year. Through nine games, his total includes 41 receptions, 545 yards, and six touchdowns. His touchdown total has doubled compared to his 2025 performance. The Ducks face three tough games to close out the regular season. They will play the Michigan Wolverines on November 14, followed by the Michigan State Spartans on November 20. A win against the Washington Huskies on November 28 will be crucial for their final standing. Oregon remains a strong candidate to win their second Big Ten title in three years. item.description: Team of the Matchday: Surridge, Rusnák deliver Decision Day drama By Justin Ruderman Stars delivered Decision Day drama to earn their spot in the Team of the Matchday presented by Audi. Full team (3-4-3, left to right) Starters: Andrew Thomas (SEA) - Mihail Gherasimencov (VAN), Lukas MacNaughton (STL), Zach Booth (RSL) - Albert Rusnák (SEA), Kaick Ferreira (DAL), Braian Ojeda (ORL), Cavan Sullivan (PHI) - Sam Surridge (NSH), Gonzalo Tapia (CLB), Liel Abada (CLT) Coach: Pablo Mastroeni (RSL) Bench: Brian Schwake (NSH), Jahkeele Marshall-Rutty (RBNY), Patrick Yazbek (NSH), Adri Mehmeti (RBNY), Nectarios Triantis (MIN), Kristoffer Velde (POR), Cheikh Sabaly (VAN), Quinn Sullivan (PHI), Robert Lewandowski (CHI) Team highlights Nashville SC broke the MLS single-season points record on Saturday, pushing their Supporters' Shield-winning total to 77 points with a 2-0 victory at FC Cincinnati , courtesy of a brace from star striker Sam Surridge . Teenage phenom Cavan Sullivan also netted twice while drawing a penalty in the Philadelphia Union 's 4-1 win over Toronto FC to cap his own record-breaking regular season. Summer signing Gonzalo Tapia helped provide the heroics for the Columbus Crew in their rollercoaster 4-3 triumph over Chicago Fire FC , scoring a pair of equalizers as the Crew went on to clinch seventh place in the Eastern Conference and avoid the Wild Card match with the win. Finishing a point behind Columbus in the table, Braian Ojeda ensured Orlando City will host the Wild Card match at Inter.co Stadium with a powerful volley off his thigh control to secure the 1-0 victory over the New England Revolution . Above them, Kaick provided the equalizing assist and winning goal for second-place FC Dallas in a 3-1 win over the Colorado Rapids , while top-seeded Vancouver Whitecaps FC ensured second priority for hosting MLS Cup presented by Audi (behind Nashville) as Mihail Gherasimencov scored in a 2-0 victory at CF Montréal . item.title: Game time set for No. 7 Texas vs. Arkansas
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 22: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns drops back from the line of scrimmage during the first half against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on November 22, 2025 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The No. 7 Texas Longhorns will host the Arkansas Razorbacks at 2:30 p.m. Central on November 21 in the final regular-season home game at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial this season, the SEC announced on Monday. The game will air on ABC or ESPN as a six-day selection. After Saturday’s win over No. 18 Missouri moved Texas to 7-2 (4-2) season, the Longhorns head back on the road this weekend for a high-profile tilt against the Tigers in Baton Rouge. The Razorbacks are struggling through their first season under Ryan Silverfield with a 3-6 record overall and a 1-6 mark in SEC play. Arkansas did notch a 31-21 conference win over Vanderbilt in addition to non-conference victories over North Alabama and Tulsa. The ESPN matchup predictor gives the Horns a 95.4-percent win probability over the Hogs. It’s the second straight matchup between the two longtime rivals in Austin, a consequence of the SEC expanding its conference schedule to nine games this season. In the all-time series that began in 1894, Texas leads 57-23.

item.title: What coach Jeff Hafley said about Miami Dolphins' loss to the Lions
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS — The Miami Dolphins once again played a strong team close but could not overcome an inept offense. The Dolphins were held to three field goals in a 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium. Miami has scored two touchdowns in its last two games and has the second lowest scoring offense in the NFL. The Dolphins (1-7) are in a good spot to pick up their second victory of the season Nov. 15 at Indianapolis. The Colts (2-7) have lost seven straight and are looking to the future, already having traded three starters for draft picks since the start of the season. More Dolphins: Dolphins trade deadline updates: Latest news, rumors, players to watch Here is what coach Jeff Hafley said Monday about the loss to the Lions (6-2). No update on quarterback Malik Willis Hafley had no update on Malik Willis' health, saying he had not met with the medical staff as of early Monday. Willis said after the Lions game he has been dealing with a lingering groin injury. Willis finished 13 of 25 for 128 yards with no touchdowns and an interception against the Lions and he was not moving as well as he was earlier in the season. When asked if Willis may need to take some time off during the week, Hafley said that decision is up to the medial staff. Hafley keeping conversations private as trade deadline looming With the NFL trade deadline Tuesday, some Dolphins veterans could be casualties of this extensive rebuilding plan and dealt for draft picks. Defensive lineman Zach Sieler, 31, and offensive lineman Austin Jackson, 27, have been mentioned in trade speculation. "I love the guys here," Hafley said. "I appreciate their effort. I love coaching every one of them. And those are my conversations with the players." When asked about his conversations with GM Jon-Eric Sullivan about the trade deadline, Hafley said: "My conversations with Sully will remain private." Dolphins treating Colts like they did Lions To many, the next game against the 2-7 Colts gives the Dolphins a great opportunity to win their second game. That is not the message Hafley is sending. "It's just not how I'm wired … it's not how we're wired," he said. "You look at an opponent like last week and you have a ton of respect for them. You watch the film and you see everything that they can do and you see all their weapons. And you work all week and you get yourself to a point where on Saturday and Sunday you go into the game. And I hope every coach and every player we have believes in that moment that we're going to win the game. "I'm not to that point where I'm just going to look at a schedule and be disrespectful. This is the National Football League. There's really good players on every team, there's really good coaches on every team. And if you don't bring it, you're not going to have a chance." item.description: What a 24-team College Football Playoff would look like in 2026 after Week 10 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After months and months of deliberation, it’s official. The College Football Playoff will be expanding to 24 teams starting in 2027. ESPN and the CFP agreed to a five-year deal worth over $1.7 billion to broadcast the expanded event. That makes 2026 the final-year of the 12-team playoff, and the race for those spots is really starting to heat up after an eventful Week 10 on Saturday. But what would happen if the 24-team playoff were being implemented this season? The biggest shift is that, in the future era of the 24-team field, conference championship games are being eliminated. That closes the door on any chance for teams to move up on championship weekend, even though most teams playing in power conference title games would be in the top 24 anyways. item.title: Blades Brown’s Win Proves 19-year-olds Can Beat The Best Right Now
item.description: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images Golf history just got rewritten by a teenager who refused to quit. Blades Brown, just 19 years old, captured his first PGA Tour title on Sunday in Mexico. He did something no one has done in 95 years. The win came after he erased a seven-stroke deficit in the final round against Ben James. This isn’t just a lucky break for a kid. It is a statement that the future of the game is here and it is aggressive. The Comeback That Shocked Everyone Most players would have folded with that kind of hole in the standings. Brown did not even blink. He closed with a nine-under 63 to force a playoff, according to the Associated Press. The final score was 23-under 265, which cleared a logjam of eight players who were all within a single stroke of one another. On the second sudden-death hole, a four-foot birdie putt secured the victory for him. Brown is now the fourth-youngest winner in tour history. He bypassed college entirely to turn pro out of high school, a move that paid off instantly. “It hasn’t set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner,” Brown said in a statement reported by Yahoo Sports . That lack of shock is exactly what makes this win so dangerous for the rest of the field. He has been thinking about this day since he was five years old. Now he is living it. At the 2023 U.S. Amateur, the kid broke a 103-year-old record, joining Tiger Woods as the only players to win the U.S. Junior Amateur and be the medalist in the U.S. Amateur in the same year. Success at this age is not an accident. Why The Old Guard Should Worry Ben James fought hard but fell short. James held a four-shot lead after 54 holes before the game got away from him on Sunday. He still managed to force the playoff with a clutch eagle on the 18th hole. James hit a 285-yard shot into 20 feet and made the putt to salvage a 70. “Had a feeling that it was going to go in,” James said of his eagle putt, per the Associated Press. But he missed an eight-foot putt on the second playoff hole while Brown made his three-footer. Last season, James held the number one spot in the PGA Tour University ranking, but he failed to stop the younger talent. The combined age of these two players in the playoff was 42, the youngest in tour history. This signals a shift in who wins on Sunday. A Masters berth is nearer for Brown at 54th globally, provided he ends the season within the top 50. Brown said with a huge grin, according to Yahoo Sports, “I’m just so obsessed with this game,”. That obsession is the difference maker. That obsession proves experience does not always beat hunger when the pressure is highest.

The latest developments follow a difficult spell for Grealish, who has missed Everton’s last four matches. The first absence came through illness, though wider attention has centred on off-field disciplinary issues and the resulting speculation over whether the club could return him to City ahead of schedule. That is not the direction Everton are currently taking. Instead, the expectation is that Grealish will rejoin the group at Finch Farm during the break, with the focus firmly on attitude, sharpness and a route back into contention before Everton’s trip to Brentford on Monday 23 November. David Moyes keeping faith in Jack Grealish There is still a strong belief inside Everton that Grealish can play a major role if he rediscovers rhythm and focus. His return of eight goal involvements in 22 games last season offered enough evidence of what he can bring when fully engaged, and that remains part of the thinking behind the club’s decision not to make a drastic move. That helps Moyes, who now has leverage as much as he has a selection issue. Grealish is not being written off, but he is being asked to earn his way back. item.description: Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham has finally revealed exactly what pushed him to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck , and apparently, it took one final look at the film to seal the deal. Speaking to reporters on Monday, Whittingham explained that he initially planned to wait until the conclusion of the 2026 season before making any major changes to his offensive coaching staff. However, after reviewing the film from Michigan’s embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, he realized waiting was no longer an option. According to Brad Galli of WXYZ-TV , Whittingham pointed directly to the regression he witnessed against the Spartans as the reason for his sudden change of heart. That explanation is particularly interesting considering what Whittingham said immediately following Saturday’s loss. At the time, he suggested he would evaluate his coaching staff after the season rather than make an immediate change. But apparently, the film told a different story. item.title: Liverpool receive new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update ahead of international break
item.description: Liverpool receive new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update ahead of international break Dominik Szoboszlai Injury Update Leaves Liverpool and Hungary Waiting Liverpool have another fitness problem to manage, and this one could carry into the international break. Dominik Szoboszlai will be assessed on Monday after coming off during the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace with a knee complaint, leaving both Liverpool and Hungary waiting for clarity. There is no point dressing it up. This is a player with a recent history of breaking down, and that matters. During the previous international break, Szoboszlai aggravated a thigh muscle issue, then lasted only 30 minutes into his return against Brentford before suffering another setback. The result was five matches missed. So when he goes off again, nobody is shrugging it off. Szoboszlai fitness concern grows Hungary now have Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland on the horizon, and his availability is clearly in doubt. The Hungarian Football Federation confirmed that checks are under way, stating: “(Dominik Szoboszlai) who was substituted in the 69th minute of Liverpool FC’s match yesterday, is undergoing tests today, Monday, following the usual protocol in such cases. We will, of course, keep the public informed of developments as soon as possible.” The timing is awkward for everyone. Liverpool want players wrapped in cotton wool, Hungary want their captain available, and Szoboszlai himself is the type who will push to play. That is often admirable, but it can also be part of the problem. Andoni Iraola offers blunt update Andoni Iraola did not pretend everything was fine. “Dom definitely wasn’t 100 per cent in the second half,” the Liverpool head coach said after the win. “Let’s see. The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. “In the last international break we lost three very important players in Alex (Isak), Cody (Gakpo) and Dom. So now I’m praying , it’s the last thing we need.” He then explained the issue more clearly: “I think Dom extended the knee a little bit. It was fine but not 100 per cent. He has to be careful to see if he can play for the international team or not. “I hope we are in a better place in two weeks. I know Dom will do everything to go as he loves to play for the national team, but he wasn’t 100 per cent when he finished the game. Hungary decision now under spotlight That leaves the medical staffs to decide what comes next. Iraola summed it up well enough: “I suppose they will have to analyse, the medical staff, and see what it is. I know what I want, but I also have to understand the national teams. “I’m sure that Dom, if he is fine he will want to go, but I’m not sure if he’s going to be fine.” For Liverpool, that final line is the one that matters most.
